## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The vow  (`#the-vow`)

Cited ayat: 3:35-36

> **3:35** إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّىٓ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
>
> **3:36** فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ وَإِنِّى سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

### Claims

**c1** (3:35): The wife of Imran said to her Lord that she had vowed to Him what was in her womb, as one dedicated to Him, and asked Him to accept it from her, for He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

**c2** (3:36): When she gave birth, she said to her Lord that she had given birth to a female.

**c3** (3:36): The ayah says that God knew best what she had given birth to, and that the male is not like the female.

**c4** (3:36): She said that she had named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan, the accursed.

### One-minute summary

The wife of Imran told her Lord that she had vowed to Him what was in her womb [c1]. When she gave birth to a female, she named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan [c2][c4].

### Complete story

The wife of Imran said to her Lord that she had vowed to Him what was in her womb, as one dedicated to Him, and asked Him to accept it from her, for He is the Hearing, the Knowing [c1]. When she gave birth, she said to her Lord that she had given birth to a female [c2]. The ayah says that God knew best what she had given birth to, and that the male is not like the female [c3]. She said that she had named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan, the accursed [c4].

### Deep study

The ayah records the words of the vow and of the naming [c1][c4]. The text does not mark whether the sentences that God knew best what she had given birth to, and that the male is not like the female, are her words or a remark added in the ayah, and readers have taken it both ways [c3].

### Kids mode

The wife of Imran asked God to accept what she had vowed to Him [c1]. She gave birth to a baby girl and named her Maryam [c2][c4]. She asked God to protect her and her children from Satan [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that she brought her vow and her newborn to God in prayer and placed her under His protection [c1][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: her name, her age or where she lived; the ayah calls her the wife of Imran.
- Not established: what the vow of dedication involved, beyond the word the ayah uses for dedicated.
- Not established: whether the words that God knew best, and that the male is not like the female, are hers or an added remark.
- Not established: how the Imran of this ayah is related to other people of that name, or when he lived.
